sections.heading: Scope
sections.text: This is a fictional procedure written for a synthetic test corpus. It does not describe any real facility. Applies to all cooling-water pumps fitted with two radial vibration sensors.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Overall vibration below 1.2 mm/s RMS is acceptable. Between 1.2 and 4.5 mm/s RMS is the warning zone: the pump may keep running while the cause is investigated. Above 4.5 mm/s RMS the pump must be stopped.

sections.heading: Reading the spectrum
sections.text: A dominant peak at shaft speed (1x) points to rotor imbalance. A peak that is not a whole multiple of shaft speed, usually between 3 and 5 times shaft speed, together with rising bearing temperature, points to a bearing defect. A raised broadband floor with no single peak, together with a drop in flow, points to cavitation; see ME-OP-022.

sections.heading: Actions
sections.text: Imbalance: schedule balancing at the next maintenance window and trend the 1x amplitude daily. Bearing defect: follow ME-MA-021. Cavitation: follow ME-OP-022.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.text: Escalate to the mechanical lead if vibration is in the warning zone on both sensors for more than 24 hours, or if the cause cannot be identified from the spectrum.

documents.title: ME-MA-021 Bearing temperature limits and inspection

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: This is a fictional procedure written for a synthetic test corpus. It does not describe any real facility. Normal bearing temperature is 45 to 55 degC. Alarm limit is 75 degC. Trip limit is 80 degC. A rise faster than 2 degC per minute at constant load is abnormal even below the alarm limit.

sections.heading: After a bearing temperature trip
sections.text: Do not restart the pump. Start the standby pump. Tag the tripped pump out of service and request a bearing inspection.

sections.heading: Inspection
sections.text: Check lubricant level and condition, then inspect the outer race for spalling. Replace both bearings as a pair.

sections.heading: Recognition
sections.text: This is a fictional procedure written for a synthetic test corpus. It does not describe any real facility. Cavitation shows as broadband vibration, a flow drop of more than 10 percent from setpoint, a lower motor current, and a SUCTION_PRESSURE_LOW alarm. The pump usually keeps running.

sections.heading: Response
sections.text: Check the supply tank level and the suction strainer. Reduce pump speed until the noise stops. Do not run a cavitating pump for more than 15 minutes.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.text: Escalate if suction pressure does not recover after the strainer is cleaned.
